items.q: Match each complement pattern with its interpretation — 1) C3↓ and C4↓ 2) Transiently low C3 3) ↓C3 with normal C4 … A) eg. PSGN B) Classical complement pathway affected, eg. MPGN Type I C) Alternate complement pathway affected, eg. C3GN, adult HUS
items.exp: C3↓+C4↓ classical (MPGN Type I); transiently low C3 eg. PSGN; ↓C3 normal C4 alternate (C3GN, adult HUS). (Book p774)

items.q: IgA deposits are seen in IgA nephropathy, IgA-predominant PSGN (adult PSGN), full house effect (SLE) and light chain deposition disease, the last showing IgA & κ light chain deposit as part of:
items.exp: Light chain deposition disease: IgA & κ light chain deposit (part of myeloma). (Book p774)

items.q: All of the following carry IgA deposits per the note EXCEPT:
items.exp: IgA deposits: IgA nephropathy, IgA-predominant PSGN, full house (SLE), light chain deposition disease; MN is not listed. (Book p774)

items.q: Fill up: The full ______ effect, listed among IgA-deposit conditions, belongs to SLE.
Which steroid-indication statement is TRUE as per this page?
opts: A high E score (endocapillary cellularity) is a steroid indication, but GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy means no steroids
Proteinuria >1 g/day at first visit mandates steroids immediately
Steroids are given lifelong in IgA nephropathy
items.exp: High E score (endocapillary cellularity) indicates steroid; GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy → no steroids; proteinuria >1 g/day only after 6 months conservative. (Book p774)

items.q: For proteinuria control in conservative management of IgA nephropathy, the drug classes written are:
items.exp: ACE inhibitor/ARBs for proteinuria control. (Book p774)
